newsitem.title: CHINA: China preparing rules for convertible bond issues.
newsitem.headline: China preparing rules for convertible bond issues.

text.p: China is drafting rules governing overseas convertible bonds to try to pave the way for more such issues and to better regulate a relatively new financial tool for mainland firms, officials said on Thursday.
The State Planning Commission was preparing the new rules and was expected to issue them before the end of the year, said Li Xuedong, an official with the commission's international finance division.
"We should draft detailed rules based on the characteristics of this fund-raising tool," Li told reporters at a symposium on convertible bonds in Beijing.
Chinese authorities have approved and regulated overseas convertible bond issues on an ad hoc basis and the new rules would unify and clarify exisiting guidelines, Li said.
"I think we can expect to issue (the rules) at the end of the year," Li said.

So far five Chinese firms with listings in either Hong Kong or on China's foreign currency B share stock market have issued approved convertible bonds overseas, raising a total of $600 million. The first approval was in 1993.

Chinese firms seeking to issue convertible bonds overseas must first obtain approval from the State Planning Commission, the Securities Commission under the State Council, or cabinet, and the State Administration of Foreign Exchange.
Li said the new rules could make it easier for more Chinese companies to issue convertible paper abroad but newcomers would still have to meet stringent requirements laid down by Beijing regulators.
"In the choice of companies there will definitely be restrictions," Li said, adding that selected firms should be engaged in a primary or pillar industry.
Analysts said that could change if more overseas convertible bonds were successful.

"The biggest problem is that issues are quite restricted now, but they are going forward and will extend to smaller companies," said Anthony Wah, head of Asian equity derivatives marketing with ABN Amro Bank.
"Because of a lack of Chinese paper, demand is definitely there," Wah told reporters.

Companies that have already issued overseas convertible bonds include light truck maker Qingling Motors Co Ltd, China Southern Glass Co Ltd, land developer China Resources Beijing Land Co Ltd, Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co and Huaneng Power.
Analysts said it was a good time for China to move ahead on issuing convertible bonds overseas because of low and stable interest rates abroad and because of China's booming stock markets.
"The market is eager for Chinese financial tools now, and this will continue," said Gu Fushen, ABN Amro Bank's corporate finance manager for China and Hong Kong.
